claim: draft_final_plan.md satisfies request.md as one coherent, executable plan, and every imported contribution is compatible and traceable to its source without material intent drift from the original handoff.

criteria.text: Dependencies and sequencing form one feasible execution order: audit before implementation, schema/security before client exposure, evaluation and product verification before activation, with explicit blocked states.
criteria.reasoning: The earlier draft01 c3 point is accepted as the repair target but rejected as a current defect. The repaired order audits before implementation, freezes the evaluation contract before prompt/runtime edits, places schema and security work before runtime/UI exposure, runs live evaluation and dedicated product verification before closeout, and enables only after all gates pass. Missing dependencies and errored evidence explicitly block acceptance.
counterevidence: candidates/plan_3.md:65 show that the audit and implementation evidence are not yet complete and that the full evaluation-first candidate placed calibration before implementation; the draft explicitly adopts contract preparation before edits while placing live evaluation after runtime integration, so these do not invalidate the stated execution order.

criteria.text: Every imported contribution from candidates 2-4 has a named source, insertion point, and compatibility rule; no contribution silently changes product intent or creates a competing status authority.
criteria.reasoning: The earlier draft01 c4 point is accepted as the repair target but rejected as an unresolved defect. The import table gives one named source, insertion point, and compatibility rule for each of candidates 2-4. The rules bound vertical slices to execution views, evaluation additions to the original section 15 contract, and security/persistence invariants to original sections 8-12. The draft also rejects competing ledgers and untraceable product requirements while preserving the original as normative.
